description:
During the 2018-19 season, the St. Louis Blues defied expectations by overcoming significant adversity. After an early-season coaching change, the Blues found their stride and carried their momentum into the playoffs. In Game 7 of the Second Round against the Dallas Stars, Patrick Maroon became an instant hero by scoring the series-winning goal in double overtime. Following an offensive zone faceoff, Robert Thomas fired a shot off the post, and Maroon, crashing the net, pounced on the rebound, knocking it in. The Blues would go on to win their first-ever Stanley Cup in that memorable playoff run.

description:
Starting in the Kings' zone, the puck transitioned to offense when Drew Doughty moved it up to Justin Williams along the boards at the center ice line. With two Devils players closing in, Williams chipped it over to a streaking Anze Kopitar. Breaking in alone on Martin Brodeur, Kopitar executed a slick deke, freezing the goalie before sliding the puck into the net. Kopitar’s Game 1 overtime heroics on the road in New Jersey gave the Kings a crucial series lead, one they never relinquished, ultimately winning in six games to capture their first-ever Stanley Cup. Kopitar was a standout during the 2012 Stanley Cup Playoffs, tying for the league lead in goals (8), assists (12), and points (20).

description:
In Game 7 of the 2019 Stanley Cup Final, the St. Louis Blues faced the daunting task of closing their first-ever championship run on the road in Boston. Holding a one-goal lead with under a minute left in the first period, Alex Pietrangelo, trailing the play, received a drop pass from Jaden Schwartz inside the Bruins' zone. Skating in on net, Pietrangelo shifted the puck to his backhand and fired it past the goalie, stunning the Boston crowd with just eight seconds remaining in the period. His goal, which would stand as the game winner, propelled the Blues into the intermission with momentum that carried through the rest of the game. Pietrangelo, the team captain, also tied for the league lead in playoff assists that season with 16.

description:
In Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Final, the Philadelphia Flyers faced the Montreal Canadiens with a chance to secure their first Stanley Cup Final appearance since 1997. Early in the first period, Flyers captain Mike Richards delivered a game-changing shift that electrified the home crowd and set the tone for the night. Down 1-0 and on the penalty kill, Richards started the sequence with a thunderous hit on a Canadiens defenseman. Moments later, as the puck was cleared into the neutral zone, Richards chased it down, diving to chip it past the Canadiens’ goalie, who had come out to play it. With the net wide open, Richards calmly backhanded the puck into the goal to tie the game with a shorthanded effort. The Flyers rode the momentum, adding three more goals in the game, with Richards assisting on two of them, sealing a 4-2 victory.

description:
Alec Martinez earned three Stanley Cups during his time with the Los Angeles Kings, but the 2014 Stanley Cup was particularly memorable for him. He scored the series-clinching goal in the second overtime of Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final. Amid chants of "We want the Cup" from the home crowd during a Kings' offensive rush, Martinez capitalized on a rebound from an initial save, firing the puck into the open net for the decisive goal. The arena erupted in celebration, with Martinez, his teammates, and the entire Los Angeles crowd sharing in the jubilation. Of the five goals Martinez scored in the 2014 playoffs, three were game winners including two in overtime.

description:
Between 2010 and 2019, Patrick Kane scored more playoff points than any player except Sidney Crosby. During that time, the Chicago Blackhawks captured three Stanley Cup championships, more than any other team. Kane produced numerous highlights throughout this dominant era, including a pivotal moment in Game 6 of the 2015 Stanley Cup Final against the Tampa Bay Lightning. With the Blackhawks up 1-0 and just over five minutes remaining in the third period, a missed Lightning shot led to a rush up the ice by Brandon Saad. After crossing the blue line, Saad dropped the puck to Brad Richards, who skated in and found Kane on the far side. Kane one-timed the puck into the net, sealing the Blackhawks' third championship in six seasons and sending the home crowd into a frenzy. Kane finished the 2015 playoffs tied for the lead in points with 23.

description:
In the 2010 Stanley Cup Playoffs, with the series tied at 2-2, Marian Hossa delivered a game-winning goal in overtime during Game 5 against the Nashville Predators, thrilling the home crowd in Chicago. As the Blackhawks pressed in the offensive zone during the first overtime period, Hossa made a crucial move to the net when the puck was cycled back to the point. A deflected shot from the point landed right on Hossa’s stick, allowing him to tap the puck into the open net for the victory. This pivotal moment marked Hossa’s first season with the Blackhawks and led to his first Stanley Cup championship. In 2020, he was honored with induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame, capping off an exceptional career.

description:
In the 2011 Stanley Cup Playoffs, facing their in-state rivals, the Los Angeles Kings, Sharks’ captain Joe Thornton scored the series-clinching goal in overtime. This dramatic goal was the only playoff overtime goal in Thornton’s storied career. During Game 6 in Los Angeles, Thornton carried the puck up the ice and advanced it into the corner. Following a scramble in front of the net, he spun around and managed to find the puck, slamming it home for the win. A former Hart Trophy and Art Ross Trophy winner, Thornton accumulated 1,539 points over his 24-season career in the NHL.

description:

The shot deflected off a defender and past the goaltender for the game winner. Chicago went on to win the Stanley Cup that year, defeating the Boston Bruins.

description:
Throughout NHL history, some of the most memorable goalie performances have come from a consistent "body of work," where a netminder wins a game or series despite being heavily outplayed, making crucial saves at key moments. But every so often, a single save stands out as both pivotal and breathtaking. Such was the case in Game 2 of the 2018 Stanley Cup Final. With the Capitals clinging to a one-goal lead and under two minutes left, Braden Holtby made an incredible diving save with the paddle of his stick, robbing Alex Tuch of what seemed like a sure goal into an open net. Holtby’s save helped Washington even the series on the road and sparked the Capitals' run of four straight wins to capture their first-ever Stanley Cup championship.

description:
In 2017, Corey Perry became the third player in NHL history—and the first since Maurice “Rocket” Richard in 1951—to score three overtime goals in a single playoff season. After sweeping the Calgary Flames in the Western Conference First Round, where Perry netted the Game 3 overtime winner, the Anaheim Ducks faced the Edmonton Oilers in the Second Round. With the series tied, Perry struck again in double overtime of a pivotal Game 5. After receiving a pass in the slot, Perry skated in, partially freezing the goalie, then patiently maneuvered around the outstretched leg to tuck the puck into the far side of the net. The former Hart Trophy and Stanley Cup winner would go on to score his third overtime goal in the following series against Nashville.

description:
In the 2012 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Philadelphia Flyers faced off against their rival, the Pittsburgh Penguins, a team they hadn’t beaten in a playoff series since 2000. With a chance to clinch the series in Game 6, Flyers captain Claude Giroux made an immediate impact. Right after the opening faceoff, Giroux delivered a massive hit on Sidney Crosby, igniting the home crowd. Moments later, in the same shift, he fired in the first goal, giving the Flyers a lead they never surrendered as they went on to eliminate the Penguins. Giroux dominated the series, leading all players with 14 points in six games. Throughout the decade beginning with the 2010-11 season, Giroux ranked 4th in the league for points and was a Top 5 finalist for the Hart Trophy in three different seasons.

In 2011, the Vancouver Canucks found themselves in a decisive Game 7 at home against the defending Stanley Cup champion Chicago Blackhawks—the same team that had eliminated them from the playoffs the year before. Alexandre Burrows, who had opened the scoring earlier in the game, became the hero in overtime. Seizing the moment after a failed Chicago clearing attempt, Burrows intercepted the puck, skated into the high slot, and unleashed a blistering slap shot that beat the goalie, clinching the series.  After their dramatic first-round victory and two more series wins, the Canucks advanced to the Stanley Cup Final, where they ultimately fell to the Boston Bruins in a hard-fought seven-game series.

description:

As the Kings applied pressure deep in the offensive zone, Anze Kopitar fed the puck back to Willie Mitchell, who fired a shot toward the net. Positioned in the slot, Dustin Brown deflected the puck past the goalie, securing the win. Three games later, the Kings captured their second Stanley Cup in three years. Brown's lone overtime playoff goal was a highlight in his remarkable 18-season career with the Kings, culminating in his No. 23 jersey being retired and raised to the rafters.

description:
In the 2017 Eastern Conference Final, Chris Kunitz scored the game-winning goal in double overtime of Game 7, propelling the Pittsburgh Penguins to the Stanley Cup Final. With the pressure mounting in the offensive zone, Sidney Crosby, who had just returned to the ice, retrieved the puck from the corner. Spotting an opportunity, Kunitz moved into position, and Crosby delivered a perfect pass. Kunitz fired a one-timer, clinching the victory and sending the Penguins to face the Nashville Predators. The Penguins ultimately won the series against Nashville in six games, securing their second consecutive championship. Kunitz was a member of four Stanley Cup-winning teams, three of which were with Pittsburgh.
